Subject: Deployment mode checklist + action items (residency & routing)

Hi Luca / Anja —

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the priority constraints. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single checklist to work from: 

Key constraints you called out:
- Production data must remain in the EU (no persistent backups or logs stored outside the EU).
- No cross-border routing to APAC for inference traffic; EU-only serving preferred.
- Procurement will need an estimated timeline and cost for both a pilot and production.
- Security needs SOC2 artifacts + network architecture before agreeing to any peering.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API (EU region): fastest to get a PoC running (hours–days). Good for pilot if we can provide EU-only logging and customer KMS integration for token-level encryption.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in EU): predictable latency/cost for production; requires commit.
3) Private VPC (customer VPC peering or on-prem): strongest residency and control; longer lead time but meets the strict residency requirement.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Finova: confirm whether a hosted EU-only PoC is acceptable for an initial 90-day pilot while procurement works on private deployment terms. (Luca / Anja)
- Finova procurement: share any hard constraints on lead time and preferred procurement vehicle (SOW vs PO). (procurement@finova-analytics.eu)
- Redwood: attach SOC2 summary + network diagram (attached). Marcus will follow up with a short tech checklist for Private/Dedicated. (Marcus / Priyom)
- Schedule security kickoff: propose Tue 9 Mar, 11:00 CET — confirm availability.

Attachments: redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf, nw-architecture-finova.vsdx, PoC-sow-template.docx

If that captures it, I’ll open the security kickoff invite and share the SOW template for procurement to fill.

— Vivek

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For production we will need Private VPC (customer-managed VPC peering) or an on-prem option — the residency requirement is non-negotiable for PII and transaction logs.
2) We are open to a short pilot in a Hosted EU region, but only if:
   - All logs and backups created during the PoC are stored in EU-only buckets,
   - We can integrate our KMS for encryption-at-rest for keys used in model request/response logs.
3) Procurement will need: an estimated cost for a 90-day hosted PoC and a separate estimate for a Dedicated vs Private production deployment; also lead times. Our procurement lead (procurement@finova-analytics.eu) is CC’d.

I’ll confirm the Tue 9 Mar security call internally and loop in our security engineer (Anja is on this thread). For the PoC, a quick checklist of required firewall rules and peering steps will help speed things up.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Deployment mode checklist + action items (residency & routing) — tech checklist

Quick tech notes to attach to the PoC / procurement estimates — added here so procurement and security get accurate expectations: 

Summary of differences and constraints:
- Hosted (EU region):
  * Pros: Fast PoC, low setup time.
  * Cons: Unless we enable customer-managed KMS and EU-storage-only configuration, some telemetry (metrics, aggregated logs) may default to our telemetry buckets. We can lock this down for a PoC with config flags.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in EU):
  * Pros: Predictable latency, no noisy neighbors, can meet stricter data retention configs.
  * Cons: Requires capacity commit and ~3–4 week lead time for allocation and testing.
- Private VPC / On-prem:
  * Pros: Strongest residency guarantees; we can ensure no egress from EU.
  * Cons: Longer lead time (6–8 weeks typical), network peering and firewall setup required; on-prem adds ops coordination.

Technical checklist for Finova (minimum items to sign off PoC):
- Provide CIDR(s) for peering and a list of IPs to allow for outbound (we'll provide exact IPs for our EU-hosted nodes).
- Confirm KMS model: customer-managed KMS with key-wrapping support (we support AWS KMS + external HSM via standard APIs).
- Data flow confirmation: confirm whether any async backups or metrics export are acceptable to leave EU (they said no) — we will disable any non-EU exports.
- SLA expectations: PoC will run best-effort; production SLA requires Dedicated or Private config (we'll include options in the quote).

Deliverables we can provide in parallel:
- SOC2 artifact pack (attached).
- Network architecture diagram tailored to Private VPC peering (attached).
- Draft SOW and timeline (we have a template link; will seed with estimates).

Estimated timelines (engineering lead estimates):
- Hosted PoC (EU-only config + KMS): ~3–7 days once we have network/CIDR and KMS info.
- Dedicated: ~3–4 weeks for reserved capacity provisioning and acceptance testing.
- Private VPC/on-prem: ~6–8 weeks including peering, security review, and acceptance testing.

Risks / open questions for sales to capture with Finova:
- Do they require continuous replica snapshots that mustn't leave the EU? (affects backup architecture)
- Any third-party model inference (partner models) that would require additional compliance checks?

I’ll draft the technical appendix for the SOW and drop it into the Drive link.

— Marcus
